newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish helicopters hit at rebel Kurd positions.
newsitem.headline: Turkish helicopters hit at rebel Kurd positions.

text.p: Turkish attack helicopters on Friday pounded Kurdish rebel camps in a remote mountain region of eastern Tunceli province, military officials said.
They said Super-Cobra helicopters launched a series of heavy raids against targets along the Alibogazi ravine, a favourite staging area of Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerrillas.

"This attack has been specifically carried out on Alibogazi in order to block the PKK's activities...in their camps at time when freedom of movement is limited by the (severe) winter," a military official told Reuter.
Army sources said rebel casualties were "heavy" but no figures were available. There was no word of any government losses.
The official said intelligence estimates put the number of PKK rebels sheltering in the area, generally out of reach of regular land forces, at about 300 fighters.

Infantry troops were on stand-by in the area to join the battle if needed, he said. However, the region's heavy snows and rugged terrain make slow going for regular troops chasing the experienced rebels.
More than 21,000 people have died in the PKK's 12-year fight for independence or autonomy in southeastern Turkey.
